title: Immunology
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Explain innate immunity, inflammation and complement, antigen presentation and MHC, T and B cells, antibodies and cytokines, hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, immunodeficiency, transplantation, vaccines and immunotherapy.

blocks.deliverable: Explain how complement deficiencies predispose to specific infections.
Compare MHC class I and II pathways.
Match antibody classes to their functions.
Week 7 midterm; classify ten conditions by hypersensitivity type.
Match immunodeficiencies to their typical infections.
Explain live versus inactivated vaccines and checkpoint inhibitors.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Immune response timeline: explain the innate and adaptive responses to a vaccine and to a bacterial infection, with the expected laboratory findings.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
